summary.title: Startup Playbook
summary.one_liner: Sam Altman's playbook distills Y Combinator's startup advice into core principles: build a product users love, assemble a strong team, grow relentlessly, and focus on execution.
takeaways: Build a product that a small number of users love before trying to reach many users; growth alone does not fix a weak product.
Evaluate the idea by how clearly it can be explained, who desperately needs it, and whether it is genuinely new (ideally 10x better) rather than derivative.
Choose a cofounder you already know well and split equity nearly equally early on; cofounder breakups are a common cause of early startup death.
Run a fast product improvement cycle by watching users closely, and recruit early users manually rather than relying on press announcements.
Keep momentum by setting a single growth metric, tracking retention rather than only signups, and sharing metrics internally.
summary.summary: This is Sam Altman's Startup Playbook, written to give Y Combinator and YC Fellowship companies a distilled set of generalizable startup advice, later published publicly. It is organized into short chapters covering the idea, founding team, product, execution, growth, focus, CEO responsibilities, hiring, competitors, money-making, fundraising, and a closing thought. The style is opinionated essay-like guidance with concrete examples (Airbnb, Facebook, Pinterest, Friendster) rather than step-by-step instructions. It is aimed at people new to startups.
